headlines.title: Do Altria's Dividends Make Up For A Lagging Stock?
headlines.summary: Selling Marlboro cigarettes and nicotine pouches generates the cash Altria Group (MO) uses to pay its dividend. Over the past year, those dividends added about 7.6 percentage points to the stock's return. Yet over a five-year timeline, the share price rose less than the S&P 500. Take a guess: once every dividend is counted, did a five-year Altria holder end up ahead of the market or behind it.

headlines.title: This Company’s Products Kill People, But It Has A 6.2% Yield
headlines.summary: Altria's cigarettes kill hundreds of thousands of Americans every year, yet its stock is quietly outperforming the S&P 500 by a wide margin in 2024. The question investors now face says as much about ethics as it does about returns.

description: Altria Group, Inc., through its subsidiaries, manufactures and sells smokeable and oral tobacco products in the United States. It offers cigarettes primarily under the Marlboro brand; large cigars and pipe tobacco under the Black & Mild brand; moist smokeless tobacco and oral tobacco products under the Copenhagen, Skoal, Red Seal, and Husky brands; oral nicotine pouches under the on! brand; and e-vapor products under the NJOY ACE brand. The company sells its products to distributors, as well as large retail organizations, such as chain stores. Altria Group, Inc. was founded in 1822 and is headquartered in Richmond, Virginia.
